assertion_audit: tests/test_bank_newton_converge.py:143 fails if the dense matrix omits an adjacent Bell node or misorders a column while step_jacobian_vector retains it, as both the pre-repair and mutated-stencil logs show; deleting the shared geometry term from both sides does not fail it.
tests/test_bank_newton_converge.py:145 fails if the dense matrix differs from step_jacobian_vector on the seeded random vector; the same shared-term omission leaves it green.
scripts/prototypes/bank_newton_converge/fresh_gate.py:116 fails only if the best fresh-read directional discrepancy exceeds 1e-3, so an error between 1e-6 and 1e-3 passes.

scripts/prototypes/bank_newton_converge/fresh_solve.py:140 fails if its best step-direction central difference exceeds 1e-3; :192 fails if a fresh read is invalid or the terminal residual exceeds 1e-10; :235-236 fail for excess axis or boundary-flux error but cannot fail for an inaccurate X-point.
No added assertion is a literal comparison of a function result to the identical value passed to that function; the matrix test instead shares the geometry mechanism between its two sides.

findings.text: Dense assembly calls the geometry tangent for every selected input channel, and that tangent runs jax.jvp at lines 467, 475, 523 and 555; this violates the no-per-step-autodiff clause and the recorded 370.02 ms warm step misses the 0.5 ms bound.

The only fresh-read directional gate accepts error below 1e-3, although the plan requires 1e-6 at trial and converged states; the recorded best trial error is 2.44e-6 and no converged-state check is present.
The oracle check computes and asserts axis and boundary-flux errors but never measures or asserts the diverted X-point error required by the locked precision budget, so a displaced saddle could pass.

The matrix-to-matvec assertion uses the same geometry tangent on both sides; removing that tangent from both functions leaves this test green, so the declared booking-derivative negative control and fresh-read convergence are not durably guarded.
